Phones in landscape are no longer treated as a squashed portrait screen: this release brings them as close to the tablet landscape layout as possible, and fixes a few problems that also showed up in portrait.

## Phone landscape

- **Docked sidebar and side panes**: the sidebar stays on the left, as on a tablet. Wide enough phones get three columns side by side; on narrower ones, opening a pane such as files or the terminal makes the sidebar step aside until the pane is closed.
- **The quick-switch row is back**: model, effort and permission under the input box used to be hidden in landscape. They're shown again.
- **Status bar hidden**: landscape gives the status bar's space back to the app. Swipe down from the top edge to bring it up for a moment.
- **Tighter spacing**: padding in the top bar, sidebar, input area and settings is trimmed, so more fits on a short screen. Nothing is taken away.
- **Full-screen settings**: settings used to shrink into a thin card on short screens. They now fill the screen, with categories on the left and content on the right.
- **Lineage shows the full metro map**: landscape used to fall back to the indented tree. It now gets the same map as a tablet, with panning and zooming.

## Fixed

- **After the first message of a new chat, the input box stayed two lines tall and pushed the send button out of place**: this happened in portrait too. The input height is now recalculated when the welcome screen goes away and on rotation.
- **The greeting stayed in the chat after the first message**: it carried Claude's name and looked like a reply. It now goes away once you send the first message.
- **With tall content, the top of the welcome screen got cut off**: the setup cards shown before a provider is configured, for example, pushed their heading off screen with no way to scroll back. Everything can be scrolled to now.
- **The model picker showed no model list on short screens**: the whole card now scrolls as one, and the model in use is listed first, so it's visible as soon as the picker opens.
- **Permission and long-press menus ran off short screens**: when they don't fit, they're capped in height and scroll on their own.
- **Dragging the lineage map all the way left left a blank strip on the right of the timeline**: the timeline background now spans the whole map.
- **A stray vertical line through the rounded corner where the docked sidebar meets the chat on wide screens**: the seam is clean now.

This release fixes a handful of interface problems, and context usage finally shows up for third-party providers.

## Fixed

- **Context stayed at 0 with third-party providers**: bridges such as claude-code-router only report real usage at the end of a response, and we only read the placeholder 0 at the start. Usage is now picked up at the start, at the end and from the full message, and reopening an old session no longer reads it as 0.
- **The greeting flickered on a new chat with interface motion off**: the screen was cleared, then redrawn once the connection came back, leaving a blank moment. It's now drawn right away and kept when the connection returns.
- **Two kinds of sidebar on wide screens**: after collapsing the sidebar, the menu button brought it back docked on the left, but swiping in from the edge opened the phone-style drawer over the chat. On wide screens it now always comes back docked.

## Improved

- **No animation when switching settings categories on wide screens**: pick a category on the left and the content on the right just changes.
- **Interface errors show where they happened**: the top bar only fits one line, so error messages got cut off. The file and line number now come first, so a screenshot is enough to find it.

Thanks to @chenshi723, who tracked down and fixed the context usage bug and reported the interface issues too.

This release is about Lineage: once you have lots of sessions, one map shows what branched from what, what each chapter did, and which session that old piece of work lives in.

## New

- **Lineage page.** A new Lineage entry in the sidebar draws all your sessions as a subway map. Time runs left to right, each line is a session, grouped into bands by project. Forks, rewinds, merges and handoffs each have their own look, and scheduled tasks appear as a dotted line. Drag with one finger, pinch to zoom time, double-tap to return to now. Tap a line to light up its family; a card at the bottom right shows where it came from and each chapter. In portrait on a phone it becomes an indented tree that just scrolls.
- **Session archiving.** Each time a session is compacted, a chapter ends and the AI in that session titles it; the session list shows the latest chapter's title. Every chapter gets an archive number like "a1b2·3" (first four characters of the session ID · chapter) that you can use to refer to it.
- **Tap a station to jump to that chapter.** On a tablet, tap a station on the map, or a chapter in the card or the session's Lineage menu, to jump to where that chapter starts. Compaction points show as a "Chapter n · title" divider. After a jump only the nearby pages are loaded and more are read as you scroll, so even sessions hundreds of MB long stay smooth. Tap the arrow at the bottom right to go back to the latest.
- **Older sessions work too.** Sessions from before this release have no archive, but their relationships are still worked out from the transcripts. Untitled chapters show their first prompt in grey, and older "go read that session and take over" handoffs are recognized. One-shot Q&As and misc sessions are hidden by default.
- **Backfill titles.** The Backfill button on the Lineage toolbar uses your global default model to title old chapters from the compaction summary at the end of each chapter, without rereading the whole transcript. Before starting it tells you the model, the number of chapters and roughly how many tokens it will use, and you can stop it at any time.
- **Tour.** "How to read" on the toolbar opens a hands-on tour with sample sessions: drag, zoom, tap a line, read chapters, tell the kinds of lines apart. There is a landscape and a portrait version.

## Fixes

- **Approval prompts with "Allow all" on.** With Allow all enabled, subagents still asked for permission before using tools. Claude Code is now started so it can switch to Allow all, and after switching, subagent tool calls are allowed too (except things that need your answer anyway, such as questions to you or leaving plan mode). Thanks to the community member who reported it.
- **Confusing "unsupported protocol" when testing an endpoint.** Some models are only offered over the OpenAI protocol by their provider, and the test returned a cryptic error. It now says plainly that the model doesn't support the Anthropic protocol, so pick another model or route (#23).
- **The "Writing parameters" count stopped moving.** With a subscription (the official API), "Writing Bash parameters · N chars" at the end of a reply often stayed stuck on the first few characters. The official API sends parameters in large chunks, and the last chunk landed inside the throttle window and was dropped. The final count is now reported when the parameters are done, and the elapsed time is shown too, so you can tell it isn't stuck even when the count holds still.
- Work Island: the title follows the current action and shows checklist progress (thanks @STUTTEFRFIX, #22).

This is a security release; please update soon. The issues came from a code audit and centre on HTML preview: opening an untrusted web page inside the app let it do more than it should.

## Fixes

- **Preview pages could read other files.** Previewing an HTML file on shared storage let its scripts climb parent folders and read all of shared storage, including photos and downloads. A preview page can now only read its own folder and the few parent levels fixed when the preview opens, and never the storage root or broad folders such as Download or DCIM. Pages that load `../assets` from a parent folder still work.
- **Preview pages could call the app's native functions.** Scripts in a preview could call uninstall, write to the clipboard or open links directly. These functions now require a key that is only given to the app's own interface, which preview pages can't get.
- **One malformed request could stop the gateway.** Any app on the device could crash the gateway with a specially crafted request. Such requests now get an error and the gateway keeps running.

## Hardening

- Downloads of Claude Code from the official source now also verify Anthropic's signature instead of relying on HTTPS alone. Older versions without a signature file fall back to the npm signature and still install.
- The interface WebView no longer has access to local files (file://).
- The in-app browser recognises local addresses more strictly, including forms like `127.1` and `2130706433`.
- The GitHub Actions used for builds are now pinned to specific commits.

This release fixes one problem: with some relay endpoints, a finished answer was taken back and written out again.

## Finished answers are no longer retracted and rewritten

- Some relays close the connection at the end of an answer without sending the final "done" signal. Claude Code treats that as a cut-off and asks the model to answer again, up to three times, and may finish with "Connection lost mid-response". On screen the answer was written, removed and written again, and the provider billed the extra calls.
- Requests to custom endpoints now go through a small local relay inside the app. When the answer has fully arrived and only the closing signal is missing, the relay adds it, so Claude Code sees a normal finish. Answers that really were cut off mid-way are left alone, and Claude Code retries them as before.
- Built-in providers and the official account don't go through this relay.

This release fixes several problems reported in the group chat and makes downloads much less likely to stall. The Claude Code version picker also starts showing which versions have been tested on a real device.

## Updates no longer stall at 0%

- When GitHub was reachable but crawling, the app kept waiting and the screen sat at "Downloading 0%". Now a route that delivers less than 600 KB in 30 seconds counts as failed and the next one is tried. If every route is slow, the download keeps going slowly instead of failing.
- App updates have a new direct route, dl.cccodroid.net (not through Cloudflare). The order is GitHub → cccodroid.net → dl.cccodroid.net → gh-proxy.
- Progress refreshes every second and shows "0 MB" at the start instead of a blank.

## No more duplicated answers

- When the connection dropped mid-answer and Claude Code retried, the half-finished first attempt stayed on screen, so the answer looked like it was written twice. The unfinished part is now removed and only the complete answer remains.

## Components page opens instantly

## Security and stability fixes

A community member did a careful code review and reported ten problems. All of them are fixed in this release:

- **The trash cleanup API could delete all app data.** A program holding the gateway token could wipe the app's home folder with one crafted request. Tapping "Empty trash" never triggered it. Names that escape their folder are now rejected, and the skill-delete API got the same fix.
- **HTML previews could reach the gateway through the native bridge.** A previewed page could use the in-app browser to open files as the gateway. Files served by the gateway can no longer run scripts, and the in-app browser and pane refuse the gateway's own address.
- **HTML previews could follow symlinks out of the preview folder.** The real path is now checked.
- **A crafted token could crash the gateway.** It is now simply rejected.
- **Chinese text or emoji occasionally turned into � while streaming.** A character split across two chunks wasn't reassembled; output is now decoded as a stream.
- **Attaching two files with the same name in the same second overwrote the first.** The second one is now renamed.
- **The editor's conflict check could miss a change made while a save was being received.** It now compares after the whole body arrives.
- **An interjection could be lost if the app was force-stopped before it was delivered.** It is now saved right away and comes back to the queue on the next launch.
- **A Claude Code update that failed its test run left you without a working version.** The new version is now tested before it's switched in.
- **Importing an archive that expands to a huge size could take down the gateway.** There is now a size limit.

**Skill import** is also fixed: every skill in an archive is installed, you can pick several files at once, archives forwarded from chat apps are no longer greyed out in the file picker, and a single SKILL.md can be imported directly.

## Fallback sources for downloading Claude Code

On some networks the official Claude Code download can't be reached, or drops halfway. First install and in-app updates now switch sources automatically:

- The official server is tried first. If it can't be reached or drops twice in a row, the app moves on to npmmirror, Tencent Cloud and the official npm registry in turn, resuming what was already downloaded. Whichever source worked last time is tried first next time.
- It's the same program either way: Anthropic also publishes Claude Code on npm, and these mirrors simply sync it.
- Wherever it comes from, the file has to match the **SHA-256 in Anthropic's official manifest** before it's installed. If the official manifest can't be reached either, the app uses the copy on cccodroid.net, which carries Anthropic's signature and is only used once that signature checks out.
- If even that copy can't be reached, the app checks npm's own registry signature, installs, and re-checks against the official manifest automatically once it's reachable again.
- The npm package is compressed, under half the size of the official direct download, so it's often faster too.

## Fixed: updating the app and the toolchain together left the toolchain "up to date" but still old

**What happened**: when the app and the development toolchain were updating at the same time, the app finished first and restarted the process, cutting off the toolchain download. After the restart, the new app used **its own built-in toolchain version** as the "installed version", so the old toolchain was shown as the new one. Confirmed on a device: what was actually installed was still devkit-2026.10.13.2 (the build before the jmod fix).

This release reworks the whole update chain:

- **Version detection**: the installed version is identified only by the content hash recorded at install time, never guessed from the app's built-in version. Installs without a record are shown as "unknown" with a suggestion to update once. Toolchains installed from a local file now have their hash recorded too.
- **Ordering**: while the toolchain is downloading or being replaced, the app update waits for it. A downloaded toolchain is installed when the app restarts, regardless of the auto-update switch.
- **Checked before replacing**: the tar hash from the release manifest is checked while unpacking; on mismatch the unpacked copy is discarded and the old toolchain is left untouched. A downloaded archive is also re-checked right before it replaces anything.
- **Recoverable replacement**: if a replacement is interrupted (app restart, process killed, battery died), the next launch finishes it or rolls back — no half-installed state. Tested on a device: killed during first-run setup, it completed on relaunch and verified clean.
- **Verify / Repair**: the toolchain now ships a per-file manifest. **Verify** in Settings checks every file's hash (35,068 files in about 4 seconds on the test device); if anything is missing or damaged, **Repair** reinstalls the same version and keeps what you installed with pip / npm -g. A quick check also runs at each launch and notifies you about missing files. Files rewritten during first-run setup (such as git-delta's completion scripts) are recorded into the local baseline by their actual content, so they are not reported as damaged.

**After upgrading**: open the app; Settings will show a toolchain update (devkit-2026.10.14.1) — update when prompted. The jmod fix arrives with it.

The pairing notification no longer uses the call category, and on startup the app posts a silent notification with the same ID and cancels it shortly after, clearing any existing ghost.
- **Toolchain: images built by jlink / jpackage would not start.** Path prefixes inside jmod files were not rewritten, so jlink reported success but the resulting `java` failed to find its libraries at launch. The fix had been committed but never made it into a toolchain build; this release ships with a rebuilt toolchain, `devkit-2026.10.14`. Existing users will be told the toolchain is out of date when they open the app — update when prompted (anything installed with pip / npm -g is kept). Archives with nothing to rewrite are now left byte-for-byte unchanged, so signed jars are no longer repacked. (From PR #6)

## Security fix (update recommended)

The gateway used to listen on 127.0.0.1 with no authentication. On Android that is not a security boundary: any app on the device with network permission, and any web page in the phone's browser, could send it requests — and `/api/chat` defaults to bypassPermissions, which amounts to arbitrary command execution on the device (and, with Shizuku installed, a path to the shell identity).

- On first start the gateway generates a 256-bit access token (stored in the app's private directory, mode 0600); `/api/*` requires it, otherwise 403
- Host is checked (blocks DNS rebinding, 421) and Origin is checked (blocks cross-site requests from web pages, 403)
- The app's UI sends the token automatically, so nothing changes for you; the token survives restarts
- Logging of rejected requests is rate-limited

## Other

- seccomp shim: a foreign SIGSYS (e.g. `kill -SYS`) is no longer swallowed and gets the default action

Open the app once after updating; old UI sessions switch to the token automatically.

First stable release. Runs the official Claude Code natively on Android phones — no root, no chroot / proot / VM.

### Highlights
- Official, unmodified Claude Code (downloaded from Anthropic's official channel and verified against the official sha256 manifest) with a GUI: streaming output, thinking, file browser, session history; you can interject while it works without interrupting the current turn
- Ways to connect: Claude account sign-in (done in the app; the browser authorization calls back automatically), Claude API key, DeepSeek / Zhipu GLM / Qwen / Kimi, and custom third-party compatible endpoints
- Toolchain (205 components from the official Termux repositories): clang 21, cmake / ninja, gdb, Python 3.14 (pip / venv), Node 26 (npm), OpenJDK 21 + aapt2 / d8 / apksigner, git / ssh and more
- **Automatic updates** (on by default; can be turned off or checked manually): Claude Code updates silently; new cccodroid versions are downloaded, signature-checked and offered for install (installed silently when idle if Shizuku is available); the toolchain is pre-downloaded on Wi‑Fi and swapped in at the next launch, keeping whatever you installed with pip / npm -g
- **One-tap Shizuku install and activation**: Settings downloads the official Shizuku (signing certificate verified) and installs it; activation goes through Wireless debugging with no computer, the pairing code is entered in a notification pinned to the top of the screen, and Shizuku re-activates automatically after a reboot (Wi‑Fi required)
- In the terminal, `priv '<cmd>'` runs commands as the shell user; `usb-adb` debugs another device over OTG; `cccodroid-selftest` exercises 71 tools one by one
- Background-freeze detection: when the system freezes the app, Settings tells you where to allow background running

### Known limitations
- arm64 only; needs about 4 GB of free space
- Vendor ROMs (measured on RedMagic) freeze background apps: allow cccodroid to run in the background and auto-start in system settings
- The default permission mode is bypassPermissions (everything allowed): the UI has no per-tool-call approval buttons yet
- `android.jar`, needed to compile APKs on the phone, is not shipped; download it yourself
- First install downloads about 830 MB; direct GitHub downloads from mainland China measured about 1 MB/s
